newsitem.title: FRANCE: France urges Turkey to withdraw troops from Iraq.
newsitem.headline: France urges Turkey to withdraw troops from Iraq.

text.p: France, expressing concern about NATO ally Turkey's attack on Kurdish rebels in northern Iraq, urged Ankara on Thursday to pull out its troops as soon as possible.
"France expresses its concern over the intervention of foreign troops in the north of Iraq, a region where the situation remains very fragile," Foreign Ministry spokesman Jacques Rummelhardt said.
"France wants Turkey to withdraw troops from northern Iraq as soon as possible, just as the Turkish authorities have declared," he told a routine briefing.

"France understands Turkey's legitimate need for security and condemns terrorism outright. But it also recalls its commitment to the territorial integrity and sovereignty of states in the region," he said.

Turkish troops, tanks and air power pounded rebel Kurdish positions inside northern Iraq in the second day of an assault by at least 10,000 troops in a remote mountainous region against camps of the separatist Kurdistan Workers Party (PKK) in Iraq.
Rummelhardt said France especially wanted Ankara to ensure respect for human rights and to ensure that civilians were not hit by the fighting.
